summary: Reactome already curates much of adipocyte biology, scattered across seven or more branches: lipolysis (Triglyceride catabolism), uncoupling (Mitochondrial Uncoupling), GLUT4 translocation, adipogenesis, leptin and adiponectin signalling, and drug-receptor events. No pathway treats adipose tissue as a tissue. The four anchors chosen by the curator sit under four different top-level pathways.

The Drareni & Seale review (2026) yields 134 claims. Of these, 55 are molecular events, 16 are groupings and 63 are cell- or tissue-level phenotypes that belong only in summations. A review cannot support an event, so the human primary literature was searched for 25 targets. Ten have direct human evidence. Several mechanisms the review presents as settled are mouse-only, and two of its claims are contested in human data: the dominant beta-adrenergic receptor in human brown fat, and ATGL as the rate-limiting lipase. A comparison with WikiPathways, KEGG and GO found topology the review does not cover: an antilipolytic Gi arm (now linked), fatty acid uptake and acyl-CoA synthesis (now linked, closing two chain gaps), and natriuretic peptide lipolysis (in the summation; offered as new reactions).

Verdict: a new pathway under Developmental Biology with four subpathways and Mitochondrial Uncoupling linked directly. Existing content is reused at the highest level that fits: 20 existing pathways are linked whole as subpathways (including Signaling by Insulin receptor, Adrenoceptors, G alpha (s) signalling events, Triglyceride catabolism and Signaling by Activin) and 7 reactions individually, with no copies and no edits. Six new reactions fill gaps with human evidence: ABHD5 activation of ATGL; ATGL hydrolysis of TAG at the lipid droplet, negatively regulated by G0S2; activin E binding its ALK7 receptor complex, and the receptor phosphorylation that connects it to SMAD2/3 signaling; and tirzepatide binding GIPR and GLP1R. A chain-continuity check found no break that needs inference from another species. Four decisions need the curator before anything is built: the parent and name, where the ATGL reactions live, coordination with colleagues' unreleased adipose work, and the activin E set edit.
rationale: The pathway is placed beside Adipogenesis under Developmental Biology because that branch already holds tissue-level topics, and 174 human pathways already have more than one parent. Existing content is linked, not copied, and at the highest level that works: whole pathways first, single reactions only where a parent pathway is mostly unrelated, and entities always. Nothing released is edited. Content already inside Adipogenesis (for example thiazolidinedione binding to PPARG) or inside a linked pathway is cross-referenced in the summations rather than linked a second time.

Events were admitted only with human primary support. Purified human protein, human receptor reconstitution and human adipocyte lines count; association studies, knockdown phenotypes and mouse-only mechanisms do not. That rule removed PRDM16 repression of QSOX1, PDGFRB suppression of IL33, the creatine and SERCA2b futile cycles, and activin E suppression of lipolysis, whose only human evidence is a preprint. It also kept the thermogenesis subpathway to existing events, because human data disagree on the receptor.

The new ATGL events reuse the instances of the existing HSL reactions (TAG and DAG at the lipid droplet, LCFA(-) and H2O in the cytosol), so their output chains straight into HSL's DAG hydrolysis. Triglyceride catabolism is linked whole, so the HSL activation steps come with it. The ATGL events sit beside it in the new subpathway, because the staging file only creates instances; moving them in is recommended (Q2).

intro: The proposal's genes, including every gene in the existing pathways it links (446 genes), were compared with 17 human WikiPathways pathways, 5 KEGG pathways (Regulation of lipolysis in adipocytes, Thermogenesis, PPAR signaling, Adipocytokine signaling, Insulin signaling) and 5 GO biological processes. 809 genes were absent; 120 appear in two or more resource types. A comparison agent grouped them into themes and checked each against gk_central. Six were actionable: two close chain gaps, one is linked, and three are new candidates. The rest are covered elsewhere (adipocyte transcription, in Adipogenesis) or out of scope.

chain_intro: Every subpathway's intended chain was checked step by step against gk_central: does an existing or proposed event connect each step to the next, through a shared entity instance or a precedingEvent? Gaps are classified as filled by existing content, needing human evidence, an inference candidate (only other-species evidence exists and the gap breaks a chain the proposal depends on), or not a break (independent events).

No inference candidate was found. Following the Curator Guide, a missing human step with only non-human evidence would be built as a non-human reaction, with a human reaction that cites it in inferredFrom. This is a last resort, used only where the missing step breaks a chain. The mouse-only steps the review describes (adrenergic induction of IL33, PDGFRB suppression of IL33, PRDM16 repression of QSOX1) would be additions rather than repairs, so they were not inferred.

hierarchy_intro: The proposed pathway gathers, under one heading, the molecular events through which human adipose tissue stores and releases lipid, produces heat, and responds to hormonal, pharmacological and stromal signals. Most of these events already exist in Reactome, spread across lipid metabolism, signal transduction, metabolism of proteins and developmental biology. The proposal therefore consists mainly of new pathway containers that link existing content, plus six new reactions where the existing content has a gap and human primary evidence fills it.

The table lists the top-level pathway, its four subpathways, the directly linked Mitochondrial Uncoupling pathway, and every member. Subpathways are ordered by physiological state: storage after feeding, release during fasting, signals acting on the tissue, and the stromal and immune niche; heat production is represented by the directly linked Mitochondrial Uncoupling. Members marked NEW are created by the staging file; members marked SHARED are existing, released Reactome events and pathways that gain this pathway as an additional parent.
topology_intro: The top-level pathway holds four subpathways and one directly linked pathway. They are not linked to one another by precedingEvent, because they describe processes that run in parallel or in different physiological states; they connect biologically through shared molecules. Cyclic AMP is the main switch: insulin lowers it through PDE3B (Adipocyte nutrient uptake and lipid storage), while catecholamines raise it through beta-adrenergic receptors (Regulated lipolysis in adipocytes), activating protein kinase A and lipolysis. Fatty acids released by lipolysis are exported to other tissues and, in brown and beige adipocytes, activate UCP1 in Mitochondrial Uncoupling (R-HSA-166187), which is linked directly under the top-level pathway. Hormones and drugs (Endocrine and pharmacological signaling) and stromal and immune signals (Stromal and immune signaling) act on these processes from outside the adipocyte.

Thermogenesis has no subpathway of its own. Its only curated content is Mitochondrial Uncoupling; its receptor step is linked once, under lipolysis; human studies disagree on the receptor (Q9); and the creatine and calcium futile cycles have mechanistic evidence only in mice (Q17). A thermogenesis subpathway would become worthwhile if the unreleased Cellular response to cold (R-HSA-9843749) is filled (Q3).

Within a subpathway, the order of events follows the curated precedingEvent links where they exist. Where a subpathway groups independent signals (the endocrine and the stromal and immune subpathways), each linked pathway carries its own internal order. Existing content is linked at the highest level that fits: a whole pathway where most of it is relevant, and a single reaction only where its parent pathway is mostly unrelated.
placement_intro: The proposal never edits existing content. Existing content is reused at the highest level that works, in this order: (1) a whole existing pathway, linked as a subpathway of the new one; (2) a single reaction, only where its parent pathway is mostly unrelated, with the reason given; (3) existing entities, always. Linked pathways and reactions gain an extra parent and stay where they are. This table shows each node's current location, its reuse level, its role here, and any change only the curator can make. The unreleased pathways at the bottom belong to colleagues and overlap this proposal (Q3).
events_intro: The proposed events are grouped by subpathway. For each subpathway, a short line shows how its events connect, followed by the draft summation and the existing events it shares. Each new reaction then gets a diagram, the reason it is proposed, its full anatomy, its draft summation, the verbatim evidence sentence with its source, and the instances the staging file creates for it.
entities_intro: Five new physical entities are proposed: two receptor complexes and the ABHD5:PNPLA2 catalyst, plus the drug tirzepatide and its two drug-receptor complexes. Every other participant reuses an existing gk_central instance, chosen so that the new reactions chain into the existing ones. Where several candidate instances existed, the one already used in the lipolysis branch was chosen, and the table says which candidates it beat.
literature_intro: Each new reaction cites primary studies only, preferring human systems: purified human protein, human receptors in cultured cells, and human adipocytes or adipocyte lines. Reviews are cited only in pathway summations. The papers considered and not used are listed below with the reason, so the exclusions can be checked.

subpathways.name: Adipocyte nutrient uptake and lipid storage
subpathways.summation: After a meal, insulin acts on adipocytes to increase glucose uptake through translocation of the glucose transporter SLC2A4 (GLUT4) to the plasma membrane (Lizunov et al. 2013), and lipoprotein lipase (LPL) releases fatty acids from circulating triacylglycerol, which adipose tissue takes up and re-esterifies (Ruge et al. 2009); in humans, uptake into adipose tissue depends on the fatty acid translocase CD36 when plasma fatty acid concentrations are low (Hames et al. 2014). Insulin also suppresses lipolysis: in human primary adipocytes it activates phosphodiesterase 3B (PDE3B), which hydrolyzes cyclic AMP (cAMP) and so lowers protein kinase A (PKA) activity on the lipolytic machinery (Rondinone et al. 2000; Jönsson et al. 2019).
topology: Signaling by Insulin receptor (R-HSA-74752) is linked whole. It carries the chain from insulin binding through IRS, PI3K and AKT2 to PDE3B, which hydrolyzes cyclic AMP and so switches off the protein kinase A signal that drives lipolysis. Translocation of SLC2A4 (GLUT4) (R-HSA-1445148) delivers the glucose transporter to the plasma membrane. Lipoprotein lipase hydrolysis of chylomicron triacylglycerol (R-HSA-174757) is reused as a single reaction, because its parent pathway is mostly about chylomicrons. Triglyceride biosynthesis (R-HSA-75109) re-esterifies fatty acids for storage.

No new reactions are proposed. The resource comparison (WikiPathways, KEGG, GO) found existing reactions for two of the chain gaps: CD36 fatty acid uptake (F4) and ACSL acyl-CoA synthesis (F5) are now linked. Their fatty acid and acyl-CoA instances differ from those of the neighbouring events, so the curator merges them (Q23). Movement of stored triacylglycerol into the lipid droplet (F6) has no Reactome event; seipin is the candidate (Q25). There is also no VLDL lipoprotein lipase event (Q13).

subpathways.name: Regulated lipolysis in adipocytes
subpathways.summation: During fasting or exercise, catecholamines bind beta-adrenergic receptors on adipocytes and raise cyclic AMP. Protein kinase A then phosphorylates hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL), as mapped in rat adipocytes (Anthonsen et al. 1998), and perilipin 1 (PLIN1), which in mouse adipocytes promotes HSL action at the lipid droplet (Miyoshi et al. 2006). In mouse adipocytes, phosphorylation releases alpha/beta hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5) from PLIN1 (Granneman et al. 2007), so that it can activate adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL, PNPLA2), which hydrolyzes triacylglycerol to diacylglycerol; HSL then hydrolyzes diacylglycerol, and monoacylglycerol lipase releases glycerol and a third fatty acid. In human multipotent adipose-derived stem (hMADS) cell adipocytes, forskolin redistributes ATGL and HSL to the same small lipid droplets and ATGL acts before HSL (Bezaire et al. 2009), whereas in human fat cells HSL contributes more than ATGL to catecholamine-stimulated lipolysis (Rydén et al. 2007). Lipolysis can also be driven independently of protein kinase A: in human adipocytes, atrial natriuretic peptide induces lipolysis through cGMP and cGMP-dependent protein kinase I, which phosphorylates HSL and perilipin (Sengenès et al. 2003). Glycerol leaves the adipocyte through aquaporin 7 (AQP7) (Kondo et al. 2002), which binds PLIN1 in human adipocytes (Hansen et al. 2016).
topology: Adrenoceptors (R-HSA-390696) is linked whole: catecholamines, and drugs such as mirabegron, bind the three beta-adrenergic receptors. G alpha (s) signalling events (R-HSA-418555) carries the receptor signal through Gs and adenylyl cyclase to cyclic AMP and protein kinase A. Triglyceride catabolism (R-HSA-163560) is linked whole: protein kinase A phosphorylates perilipin 1 and hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL), HSL dimerizes, binds FABP4 and moves to the lipid droplet, and perilipin 1 releases ABHD5.

The antilipolytic arm, found by the resource comparison, is linked beside it: Adenosine P1 receptors (R-HSA-417973) and Hydroxycarboxylic acid-binding receptors (R-HSA-3296197) bind their ligands, liganded Gi-coupled receptors bind Gi (R-HSA-749456), and Gi inhibits adenylyl cyclase (Adenylate cyclase inhibitory pathway, R-HSA-170670), opposing the Gs arm. The alpha2-adrenergic receptors in Adrenoceptors belong to the same arm. A second pro-lipolytic arm, natriuretic peptide signaling through cGMP and PKG1, has human evidence but no Reactome events connecting it to the lipases (Q24).

The two new reactions fill the gap at the start of triglyceride hydrolysis. Today Reactome releases ABHD5 from perilipin 1 (R-HSA-163539) but never uses it, and HSL is the only lipase acting on lipid-droplet triacylglycerol. In the proposal, ABHD5 binds ATGL (E1); the ABHD5:ATGL complex hydrolyzes triacylglycerol to diacylglycerol (E2), with G0S2 as a negative regulator; and the diacylglycerol produced is the same instance HSL already hydrolyzes (R-HSA-163402). Monoacylglycerol lipase then releases glycerol (R-HSA-163595), which aquaporin 7 exports (Transport of glycerol from adipocytes to the liver by Aquaporins, R-HSA-432030).

Two linked pathways sit beside the chain: the curator's anchor NR1H2 & NR1H3 regulate gene expression linked to triglyceride lipolysis in adipose (R-HSA-9031528), which controls expression of the lipolysis genes, and Lipid particle organization (R-HSA-8964572), which holds the lipid droplet structural proteins.

Antilipolytic: adenosine and hydroxycarboxylic acids bind their receptors → Gi → adenylyl cyclase inhibited.

subpathways.name: Endocrine and pharmacological signaling in adipose tissue
subpathways.summation: Adipose tissue receives hormonal signals from the gut, liver and muscle, and secretes the hormones leptin, whose serum concentration rises with fat mass in humans (Considine et al. 1996), and adiponectin, which is paradoxically decreased in human obesity (Arita et al. 1999). Activin E, a disulfide-linked homodimer of the inhibin beta E subunit (INHBE) expressed mainly in liver (Hashimoto et al. 2002), signals through the type I receptor ALK7 (ACVR1C) and activates SMAD2/3 in mouse adipocytes (Vestal et al. 2024); loss-of-function variants in INHBE are associated with a favorable fat distribution and lower risk of type 2 diabetes (Deaton et al. 2022; Akbari et al. 2022). The incretin gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) acts through its receptor GIPR, which single-nucleus data place mainly in pericytes and mesothelial cells of adipose tissue, although cultured human adipocytes respond to GIP (Timper et al. 2013; Campbell et al. 2022; Regmi et al. 2024). Tirzepatide is a dual agonist of GIPR and the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP1R) (Willard et al. 2020). Blocking the interleukin-6 (IL6) receptor in humans prevented the exercise-induced loss of visceral adipose tissue (Wedell-Neergaard et al. 2019). Thiazolidinedione binding to PPARG is described under Transcriptional regulation of white adipocyte differentiation.
topology: This subpathway groups three sets of signals. (a) Liver to adipose: activin E (the INHBE homodimer) binds the receptor complex ACVR2A,B:ACVR1C (E3, new), and ACVR2A,B then phosphorylates ACVR1C (E6, new). The phosphorylated complex is the input to the existing SMAD2/3 phosphorylation in Signaling by Activin (R-HSA-1502540), which is linked whole, once the curator adds it to the catalyst set (Q19). (b) Incretins and incretin drugs: GIP binds GIPR (R-HSA-420274) and GLP1R agonists bind GLP1R (R-HSA-9728664), both reused as single reactions because their parent pathways are mostly unrelated; tirzepatide binds both receptors (E4, E5, new); the curator's anchor Synthesis, secretion, and inactivation of GLP-1 (R-HSA-381771) is linked for context. (c) Adipokines and myokines: Signaling by Leptin (R-HSA-2586552) and Interleukin-6 signaling (R-HSA-1059683) are linked whole; adiponectin binding its receptors (R-HSA-8848663) is reused as a single reaction.
Thiazolidinedione binding to PPARG is already under Adipogenesis, so it is cross-referenced in the summation, not linked.

subpathways.name: Stromal and immune signaling in adipose tissue
subpathways.go_bp: none proposed: no single GO BP covers the niche (Q12)
subpathways.summation: Mesenchymal stromal and immune cells influence whether adipose tissue expands healthily. Human adipose stromal cells and adipocytes express interleukin-33 (IL33) (Wood et al. 2009), and group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s), which depend on IL33 in mice, are present in human white adipose tissue and are reduced in obesity (Brestoff et al. 2015). Transforming growth factor beta (TGF-beta) inhibits the differentiation of human adipocyte precursor cells (Skurk et al. 2006).
topology: Interleukin-33 signaling (R-HSA-9014843) and TGF-beta receptor signaling activates SMADs (R-HSA-2173789) are linked whole. They represent the stromal and immune signals with human support: IL33 from adipose stromal cells acting through IL1RL1 and IL1RAP, and TGF-beta-1 signaling to SMAD2/3. The curator's anchor Biosynthesis of protectin and resolvin conjugates (R-HSA-9026766) is linked as the pro-resolving lipid-mediator context. No adipose-specific evidence was found for it (Q10).

The review's adipose-specific mechanisms here, such as PDGFRB-mediated loss of IL33, fibro-inflammatory progenitors, and macrophage transfer of mitochondria, have been shown only in mice. They are therefore described in the summation rather than curated as events.
subpathways.flow: Interleukin-33 signaling (IL33 → IL1RL1 → IL1RAP); TGF-beta receptor signaling to SMAD2/3; PCTR/RCTR biosynthesis for context. All shared; none new.
subpathways.figure: Fig. 2C (IL-33-producing MSCs, ILC2s); Fig. 3A (TGFβ-SMAD); Fig. 3C (PDGFRβ, IL-33)

events.summation: Once released from perilipin 1 (PLIN1), alpha/beta hydrolase domain-containing protein 5 (ABHD5, also known as CGI-58) binds adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL, PNPLA2) at the lipid droplet and stimulates its triacylglycerol hydrolase activity up to 20-fold in cell-based assays. ABHD5 alleles carrying mutations found in Chanarin-Dorfman syndrome fail to activate ATGL, and functional ABHD5 restores lipolysis in fibroblasts from patients with the syndrome (Lass et al. 2006). In human multipotent adipose-derived stem (hMADS) cell adipocytes, ATGL and ABHD5 act before hormone-sensitive lipase in the stepwise hydrolysis of triacylglycerol (Bezaire et al. 2009).

events.summation: At the lipid droplet, adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL, PNPLA2) activated by ABHD5 hydrolyzes triacylglycerol (TAG) to diacylglycerol (DAG) and a long-chain fatty acid, the first step of lipolysis. Purified human PNPLA2 has TAG lipase activity (Jenkins et al. 2004), and in human multipotent adipose-derived stem (hMADS) cell adipocytes ATGL overexpression increases whole-cell lipolysis and ATGL acts before hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) (Bezaire et al. 2009). The DAG produced is the substrate of HSL. G0/G1 switch protein 2 (G0S2) binds the patatin-like domain of ATGL and inhibits its TAG hydrolase activity (Yang et al. 2010); in human Simpson-Golabi-Behmel syndrome (SGBS) adipocytes, G0S2 overexpression reduces and G0S2 silencing increases lipolysis (Schweiger et al. 2012).

entries.topic: Where the new pathway hangs
entries.position: Do not create a new TopLevelPathway. Make Adipose tissue remodeling a sibling of Adipogenesis under Developmental Biology, optionally with a second parent, Integration of energy metabolism.
entries.evidence: No existing pathway treats adipose as a tissue-level topic.
